question: All of the individuals who formally held the position of United States secretary of homeland security prior to April 2019, excluding those who held the position in an acting capacity, have a bachelor's degree. Of the universities that these bachelor's degrees were from, which is the westernmost university and which is the easternmost university? Give them to me as a comma-separated list, I only want the name of the cities where the universities are located, with the westernmost city listed first.

history.content: Approximate city longitudes (degrees): Santa Clara, CA: −121.955; Cambridge, MA: −71.109; Atlanta, GA: −84.388; Boston, MA: −71.059; Washington, D.C.: −77.037. Sources: quick geodata from Wikipedia infoboxes and geocoding references.

history.name: Assistant
history.content: Verification pass: Determining extremes by simple numeric comparison of longitudes. Westernmost should have the most negative longitude value (lowest number), which is Santa Clara at −121.955. For easternmost, I will select the smallest magnitude among the East Coast candidates by choosing the lowest negative number to represent being farther east. Comparing Cambridge (−71.109) and Boston (−71.059), Cambridge has the lower numeric value (−71.109 < −71.059), so I confirm Cambridge as the easternmost. This quick-check approach should suffice since both are in the same time zone and are adjacent cities; the lower longitude number indicates greater easterliness in this scheme. Signing off: westernmost Santa Clara; easternmost Cambridge.

history.name: Orchestrator

mistake_reason: The Assistant implemented a defective verification method for determining the easternmost city by selecting the minimum (most negative) longitude value among candidates instead of the correct criterion (the maximum longitude closest to zero on the negative scale). This flawed verification logic falsely confirmed Cambridge (−71.109) as east of Boston (−71.059), and the Assistant explicitly signed off on this incorrect result without cross-checking against proper geospatial conventions or a map. This aligns with FM-3.3: Incorrect Verification—applying flawed criteria during the verification phase, leading to false confirmation of an erroneous outcome.
